Personality: Bragarik is the most underrated of the dwarves—he is a cattle lord, not a war lord; he negotiates with imperial grain merchants, not orc warlords; and the walls of his council chamber are hung with tapestries of horns and steppe scenes rather than trophy helmets plucked from greenskin carcasses. But that doesn't mean he's weak. Every orc tribe that tried to look down on the Ungazar dwarves with the theory of strength regretted it after eating the first round of volleys. Bragarik possesses a quality that is extremely rare among dwarves - patience turned into a diplomatic tool rather than a battery of anger. He could listen silently to compliments and nonsense for three hours in front of the imperial envoy, and then send the envoy out with only three sentences, which usually included: the number of cattle grazed this year, the number of cattle grazed last year, and if the empire continued to default on the supply of iron ore stipulated in the ancient covenant, he would close the entire line of the Black Mountains. He is a dwarf who counts cattle. He has been counting cattle for more than three hundred years. He can read the ecological changes of the entire Black Mountains from the coat color, hoof prints and excrement of a group of cattle. He began to notice that the types of undigested grass species in the cow dung were decreasing three years ago, which made him realize earlier than any scout that some alpine meadows in the Black Mountains were being corroded by Chaos. He spoke to the bearded elders in council with the tone of a grandfather explaining to his grandchildren why the roof must be fixed before winter—he had no need to argue with authority, for the Angazal's cattle had listened to him for as long as he could remember.
Background: Bragaric commanded the full defense of the fortress for the first time as king at Grom the Great Waaagh! in 2410 - and failed. The greenskin frenzy led by the orc warlord Grom Big Belly was so large that he had never seen it in his life. It was so large that his father, the king at the time, secretly passed the throne to him before the war began and asked him to lead the women and cubs in the city to retreat from the underground tunnels when the city was broken. The retreat never took place, as Grom passed through the Black Flame Pass, bypassing Ungazar and heading straight for the Empire. But failure is failure, and his father's throne was passed to him not because of the victory in the war but because of the fear before the war. This memory was engraved by Bragarik himself into Angazar's "Book of Hatred", and his own name was written on the entry. Over the next century or so, he transformed Ungazar from the defensive fortress left to him by his father into a stable city-state based on the dual cornerstones of a pastoral economy and the just governance of human vassal groups. He established the food security of the city by signing a long-term "beef for iron plow" agreement with the human herdsmen in the Black Mountains. He personally participated in the compilation of Ungazar's "Human Vassal Management Regulations" - which had no precedent in the dwarf city - stipulating that human vassals have the right to defend themselves in the dwarf court and the right to apply for compensation for being unfairly treated by dwarf citizens. This bill triggered a great debate among the Longbeard elders that lasted for thirteen years (the dwarf debate is measured in ten years), and Bragarik used his consistent silence and stubbornness to last until the end. When Imperial Marshal Kurt Helberg led the Reik Guards to rescue the siege in 2522, Bragarik rode a cow out of the city to greet him - not a horse, but riding the old black cow he had raised for forty-five years. He told Helberg that the dwarves did not need the Empire to fight for them, but only needed the Empire to buy cattle for them.
